title: Spark nets its Upkeep Rebate against the fees it owes rather than claiming it as a separate payment
content:
Two short provisions define how the rebate is actually taken. A.6.1.1.1.2.3.2.2.1.2.1.1: "Spark keeps all tokens of other Agents it holds in its SubProxy account." A.6.1.1.1.2.3.2.2.1.2.1.2: "When paying Ecosystem Upkeep fees, Spark deducts the rebate from the fees it pays."

The first makes the rebate base observable. Because peer-Agent holdings are concentrated in one known on-chain account, the quantity the rebate depends on can be verified by anyone rather than asserted by Spark. Custody discipline is doing accounting work here.

The second chooses netting over a separate claim. A rebate paid out as its own transfer would require a disbursement process, a budget line and an approval; deducting it at payment time avoids all three. The cost is that the paying party computes its own reduction, so the fee arrives already net of a number Spark chose.

That is precisely why the next provision installs a reviewer: the rebate calculation is checked by Operational GovOps before surplus is returned to token holders. Self-assessment is made workable by after-the-fact verification against a publicly inspectable account, not by trust.
description: All peer-Agent tokens are held in Spark's SubProxy account and the rebate is deducted at payment time, making the rebate a self-calculated reduction that must be checked afterwards.
